title: P-1: inject obligation-source policy via the set manifest (accessor functions — co-residency safe)
recipe: SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §5 P-1 (FD-7) as REVISED 2026-08-01 by ruling R3 (co-residency) — the export-shape choice is no longer open: option (b) accessor FUNCTIONS is forced. Platform work; no recipe doc exists yet (docs/add-a-set.md is authored by pp-053, AFTER this increment) so §5 P-1 + §4.2 row 9 of the plan IS the script.

filesToTouch.what: Add one export beside the existing accessors: `export const policy = () => (store.has(currentSetId()) ? (store.current().policy ?? {}) : {})`, where `store` is the per-set `setKeyed('obligation set')` registry that pp-056 (P-9) installed in this file and `currentSetId` comes from '../../shared/set-context.js'. Deliberately NOT via requireConfiguredSet(): an unresolvable set context, an unconfigured set, or a configured set with no `policy` member all yield {} (empty-safe defaults per §5 P-1), so L2 units that never configure a set stay green. Wrap the currentSetId() call so its FD-17 'No set context' throw (raised only when two or more sets are mounted with no active context) degrades to {} here rather than propagating out of a policy read — record that as a deliberate local softening; every OTHER manifest accessor keeps throwing. No other change to this file (P-9 already keyed it).

OPTION (b), forced by co-residency. Delete the four module-load literal declarations (SYSTEM_POPULATED line 29, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE lines 31-34, MAX_ENTRIES_FROM lines 41-43, SYSTEM_ANSWER_KEYS line 70) and the SCREAMING_SNAKE export names with them. Import { policy } from '../model/obligations/manifest.js'. Add four accessor FUNCTIONS, each deriving from the CURRENT set's policy on EVERY call (nothing cached, nothing computed at module load): `export const systemPopulated = () => new Set(policy().systemPopulated ?? [])`; `export const enforcedAtContinue = () => new Set(policy().enforcedAtContinue ?? [])`; `export const maxEntriesFrom = () => policy().maxEntriesFrom ?? {}`; `export const systemAnswerKeys = () => new Set(policy().systemAnswerKeys ?? [])`. Set/object return types are chosen so each consumer body changes by exactly one token pair (`SYSTEM_POPULATED.has(x)` → `systemPopulated().has(x)`). A cached one-shot 'lazily-derived view' keeping the old names is FORBIDDEN: a view resolves once per process, but under co-residency the correct value differs per REQUEST, so a cached view would serve live-animals' enforcedAtContinue to a plant request. Rewrite the cap comment (currently 'only the declaration lives here') to state, present tense, that the declaration lives on the set manifest's policy.maxEntriesFrom. After the edit, grep this file for any obligation-name literal (poApprovedReferenceNumber, countryOfOrigin, commoditySelection, animalIdentifiers, numberOfAnimalsQuantity, referenceNumber) must return nothing.

New unit test (input/output, no mocks). Four describes: (1) SINGLE-SET derivation — a synthetic manifest `{ obligations: [], groups: [], policy: { systemPopulated: ['fieldA'], enforcedAtContinue: ['fieldB'], maxEntriesFrom: { things: 'thingCount' }, systemAnswerKeys: ['customRef'] } }` passed to configureObligationSet('synthetic', …) and read under withSetContext('synthetic', …): systemPopulated().has('fieldA') true / has('poApprovedReferenceNumber') false; enforcedAtContinue().has('fieldB') true; maxEntriesFrom().things === 'thingCount' and .animalIdentifiers undefined; unrecognisedAnswerKeys({ customRef: 'x' }) === [] while unrecognisedAnswerKeys({ referenceNumber: 'x' }) flags it. (2) EMPTY-SAFE — a manifest with NO policy member: all four accessors return empty Set/{} and nothing throws; likewise when no set context is resolvable. (3) LIVE-ANIMALS derivation — the real manifest yields today's four surfaces exactly. (4) **CO-RESIDENCY (the assertion the pre-reversal plan could not write)** — registerSetMount two ids, configureObligationSet each with a DIFFERENT policy, then in ONE process assert `withSetContext('a', () => [...enforcedAtContinue()])` and `withSetContext('b', () => [...enforcedAtContinue()])` return different arrays, and that interleaving the two reads does not bleed. This is the unit-level per-set proof; the HTTP-level version is added to co-residency.test.js by pp-006. afterEach restores the live-animals configuration and clears any test mounts (the vitest setupFile configures live-animals once per worker and other tests rely on it).

The count-cap step (~line 298) shows `export const MAX_ENTRIES_FROM = { animalIdentifiers: 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' }` living in bridge/obligation-source.js. Rewrite the snippet + surrounding sentence: the cap is declared on the set manifest — `policy.maxEntriesFrom = { animalIdentifiers: 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' }` in sets/live-animals/obligations/index.js — and read through bridge/obligation-source.js's `maxEntriesFrom()` accessor; enforcement (cardinality.js collectionCapAt, appendEntryAt rejecting at the cap) unchanged.

If the reference is link-only and already accurate, leave the file unchanged.

notes: AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency). SCOPE HARDENED — this is the change of record: the round-1 plan of this increment chose a HYBRID of option (a) (keep the SCREAMING_SNAKE export names as lazily-derived one-shot membership views so eight import sites compiled untouched). **That option is now DEAD.** A lazily-derived view resolves ONCE per process; under co-residency the correct value differs per REQUEST, so a cached view would serve live-animals' ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE to a plant-products request. P-1 therefore takes option (b) — four accessor FUNCTIONS evaluated on every call — which puts EVERY file in the 10-strong consumer list in scope. There is no smaller option; sizeGuess rises M→L accordingly. NEW DEPENDENCY: pp-056 (the P-9 set-context increment) must land first, because policy() reads the per-set obligation-set registry through currentSetId(); before P-9 there is nothing per-set to read. ID CONVENTION for the four increments the reversal adds (used across the amended files so the graph stays acyclic): pp-056 = P-9 set-context module + per-set seam keying; pp-057 = P-10 per-set URL namespace; pp-058 = P-11 setId-first convention tripwire; pp-053 = G-A/R6 author src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md. The two consumers needing most care are flow/dispatch.js:3,77 (runs at BOOT inside buildDispatch, so it resolves the set being built via the gateway's withSetContext wrapper) and sets/live-animals/.../flow/entry-guard.js (runs PER REQUEST inside the realm-scoped guard) — neither may capture an accessor result outside its call. Return-type choice (headless decision): systemPopulated/enforcedAtContinue/systemAnswerKeys return Sets and maxEntriesFrom returns a plain object, so each consumer body changes by one token pair rather than being restructured — smallest honest diff, no Proxy magic, explicit names per house style. Empty-safe ruling retained and widened: policy() returns {} for an unconfigured set, a set with no policy member, AND an unresolvable set context (FD-17 throws only when 2+ sets are mounted with no active context; a policy read degrades to {} rather than propagating that). Every OTHER manifest accessor keeps throwing — the softening is local and deliberate. bridge/scope.js is now an EDIT (it was 'no edit' in round 1): its comment names ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE, a name that ceases to exist. CO-RESIDENCY ACCEPTANCE SPLIT: §5 P-1 requires the co-residency suite to prove the two sets read different enforcedAtContinue values in one process, but co-residency.test.js is CREATED by pp-006 (P-3), which lands after this increment in the §9 m0-a order. This increment therefore proves per-set divergence at the unit level (two configured set ids + withSetContext, no server needed) and hands the HTTP-level assertion to pp-006, whose acceptance now names it explicitly. Two-sided verification rule (REVISED, R3): 'both sets serve from one process' cannot be exercised here — no plant files exist and only live-animals is mounted — so the bar for this increment is FD-17's sole-set fallback keeping the ENTIRE existing suite green with only mechanical edits, plus the unit-level two-set proof above. Exemplars: model/obligations/manifest.js accessor style; bridge tests that compose a synthetic set (fulfilments.characterisation.test.js pattern). Rulings applied: R3 (co-residency reverses SD-9/FD-1/FD-2/FD-4), FD-7 (policy on the manifest via the existing seam), FD-14/FD-17 (set-context + sole-set fallback), §4.2 row 9, §5 P-1 as revised. Memory rails: no migration comments, comments describe present behaviour only, test on input/output, no coverage-padding tests.
